sourceEvidence.claim: The ART intro block — initiation, indications, the 3-drug backbone, the HIV-2 exceptions, PrEP
sourceEvidence.quote:
Antiretroviral therapy (ART): often initiated at the time of HIV diagnosis.
Strongest indication for use with patients presenting with AIDS-defining illness, low CD4+ cell
counts (<500 cells/mm3), or high viral load. Regimen consists of 3 drugs to prevent resistance:
2 NRTIs and preferably an integrase inhibitor.
Most ARTs are active against both HIV-1 and HIV-2 (exceptions: NNRTIs and enfuvirtide not
effective against HIV-2).
Tenofovir + emtricitabine can be administered as pre-exposure prophylaxis.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: NRTI MECHANISM — competitive inhibition, chain termination, no 3' OH; tenofovir the nucleoTide; all phosphorylated; ZDV prophylaxis and pregnancy; the source's own in-cell mnemonic
sourceEvidence.quote:
Competitively inhibit nucleotide binding to
reverse transcriptase and terminate the DNA
chain (lack a 3′ OH group). Tenofovir is a
nucleoTide; the others are nucleosides. All
need to be phosphorylated to be active.
ZDV can be used for general prophylaxis and
during pregnancy to ↓ risk of fetal transmission.
Have you dined (vudine) with my nuclear
(nucleosides) family?
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: NRTI ADVERSE EFFECTS — myelosuppression with G-CSF/erythropoietin rescue, nephrotoxicity, the HLA-B*5701 abacavir contraindication
sourceEvidence.quote:
Myelosuppression (can be reversed with
granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
[G-CSF] and erythropoietin), nephrotoxicity.
Abacavir contraindicated if patient has
HLA-B*5701 mutation due to ↑ risk of
hypersensitivity.

sourceEvidence.claim: NNRTI MECHANISM — different site, no phosphorylation, no nucleotide competition
sourceEvidence.quote:
Bind to reverse transcriptase at site different
from NRTIs. Do not require phosphorylation
to be active or compete with nucleotides.

sourceEvidence.claim: Integrase strand transfer inhibitors — the full card (reversible integrase inhibition; increased creatine kinase, weight gain)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Integrase strand transfer inhibitors
Also called integrase inhibitors. Inhibit HIV
genome integration into host cell chromosome
by reversibly inhibiting HIV integrase.

↑ creatine kinase, weight gain.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Protease inhibitor MECHANISM — virion maturation, the pol-gene protease, boosting requirement, the source's own in-cell mnemonic
sourceEvidence.quote:
Prevents maturation of new virions. Maturation
depends on HIV-1 protease (pol gene), which
cleaves the polypeptide products of HIV
mRNA into their functional parts.
All protease inhibitors require boosting with
either ritonavir or cobicistat.
Navir (never) tease a protease.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Protease inhibitor ADVERSE EFFECTS — the metabolic set, GI intolerance; the rifampin CYP/UGT-induction interaction with rifabutin substitution; ritonavir only as booster
sourceEvidence.quote:
Hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, lipodystrophy
syndrome, GI intolerance (nausea, diarrhea).
Rifampin (potent CYP/UGT inducer) ↓ protease
inhibitor concentrations; use rifabutin instead.
Ritonavir (cytochrome P-450 inhibitor) is only
used as a boosting agent.
